question: Your team's monorepo contains a payments package and a web frontend package, and a shared standards/ folder holds files such as api-conventions.md, pci-security.md, and accessibility.md. The root CLAUDE.md currently includes all of these standards, and Claude Code often applies payment security rules while editing frontend components. Each package maintainer knows which standards apply to their package. How should you configure CLAUDE.md so that each package receives only its relevant standards?

options.text: Have each developer add @import references to all standards files in their user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md file for consistent guidance.
options.reason: User-level instructions apply only to that user and are not shared through version control, and importing every file is not selective by package.

options.text: Remove the standards from CLAUDE.md and ask developers to paste the relevant standards text into their prompts at each session start.
options.reason: Manual pasting is not shared project configuration and gives inconsistent results; the guide uses project-level CLAUDE.md files with @import to deliver standards to the team.

options.text: Add @import references for every standards file to the root CLAUDE.md so that all packages receive the complete set of standards.
options.reason: This loads every standard into every package, so the frontend still gets payment security rules; the guide calls for selective imports per package.

options.text: Have each package maintainer add @import references in that package's CLAUDE.md for only the standards files relevant to that package.
options.reason: The guide describes using @import in each package's CLAUDE.md to selectively include relevant standards files, based on the maintainer's domain knowledge.
